note: Single source of truth for the layer rules. Consumed by .claude/hooks/brick_check.py and the /brick-check command. Change limits HERE, nowhere else. Regexes deliberately use [x] character classes instead of backslash escapes so they survive JSON encoding unambiguously.

layers.role: Pure conversion rules: rows as the converter sees them, column/row-to-SubmodelElement mapping, idShort rules, document outline. No I/O.
Protocols only. No implementations, no logic.
Use-cases: convert a workbook to an AASX, render an AASX to AsciiDoc, compile AsciiDoc to PDF. Orchestrates domain through ports.
Everything that touches the outside world. One sub-package per concern (excel, aasx, asciidoc, pdf, web, cli).
Settings (upload limits, Asciidoctor binary/theme, paths), read and validated once at startup.
Composition root. The ONLY module allowed to construct adapters and wire them to use-cases.

pureLayerNote: A pure layer may import the standard library except the I/O modules above, plus its allowed layers. Any third-party package (openpyxl, basyx, lxml, ...) is I/O or a technology choice and belongs behind a port.

budgets.exportsExemptNote: Every test function is a public name; the exports budget measures a module's API surface, which test modules do not have.
budgets.functionLocExemptNote: The function-length budget detects a sequence of unnamed steps hiding inside one function. A test class groups many small independent cases; splitting it would scatter related tests for no gain. Security rules, layering and file size still apply to tests.

forbidden.reason: AASX packages are untrusted ZIPs. extractall follows ../ and absolute member names (zip slip) and has no size cap (zip bomb). Read members by name through the AASX adapter, or extract one member at a time after validating its resolved path and size.
User-edited AsciiDoc and uploaded filenames reach the Asciidoctor call. Pass an argument list, never a shell string.
AsciiDoc from the web editor is untrusted. UNSAFE mode lets include:: read any server file and lets docinfo/scripts run. Use secure mode; whitelist what the template needs.

escapeHatch.note: Append `# arch-allow: <written reason>` to the offending line to override a blocking rule. The written reason is required and shows up in review.
